classification.difficultyReason: Part a scaffolds the key reframing: x labels the whole chord EF, so PF = x - 3 by subtraction. Part b then applies the intersecting-chords product with the intercepts 3(x-3) = 6×4 and solves a simple two-step linear equation. This is slightly harder than p37-q1-t, where the unknown is a single intercept and 6x = 45 is immediate. It is easier than p37-q1-u, which needs an unlabelled intercept found by chords and then Pythagoras with a right-angle link. The hardest essential demand is a routine linked procedure: one theorem application plus an expression, with the setup supplied.

answer.worked:
The products of the intercepts of intersecting chords are equal.
$$\begin{align*}3(x-3)&=6\times4\\3x-9&=24\\3x&=33\\x&=11\end{align*}$$
